preconditions.expression: n == int(stdin.split()[0]) and len(stdin.split()) == 2 and len(stdin.split()[1].split()) == n
preconditions.description: stdin consists of exactly two lines: first line is an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 4⋅10^5), second line contains exactly n space-separated integers (1 ≤ a_i ≤ 10^9).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(num) <= 10**9 for num in stdin.split()[1].split())
preconditions.description: All integers in the input list satisfy 1 ≤ a_i ≤ 10^9.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip().split() and stdout.count('\n') == 2 + int(stdout.split()[0]) and int(stdout.split()[0]) <= n
postconditions.description: stdout consists of exactly three lines: first line is x (1 ≤ x ≤ n), second line is p and q (p * q = x), and the next p lines form a p×q matrix with x distinct integers from the input.

postconditions.expression: all(len(row.split()) == int(stdout.split()[1].split()[1]) for row in stdout.strip().split()[2:])
postconditions.description: Each of the p lines in the matrix has exactly q space-separated integers.

postconditions.expression: all(all(a != b for a in row.split()) for row in stdout.strip().split()[2:]) and all(all(a != b for a, b in zip(*[row.split() for row in stdout.strip().split()[2:]])))
postconditions.description: The matrix is beautiful: all values in each row and each column are distinct.

postconditions.expression: set().union(*[set(row.split()) for row in stdout.strip().split()[2:]]) <= set(stdin.split()[1].split())
postconditions.description: All integers in the matrix are present in the input list.

postconditions.expression: int(stdout.split()[0]) == max(x for x in range(1, n+1) if any(p*q == x and p <= n and q <= n and all(all(a != b for a in row) for row in matrix) and all(all(a != b for a, b in zip(*matrix)) for matrix in generate_matrices(x, p, q, stdin.split()[1].split()))))
postconditions.description: The output matrix has the maximum possible number of cells (x) among all possible beautiful rectangles constructible from the input integers.
